answer: One concrete defense is a bonded harbor: every agent must lock a stake in a shared escrow before it can transact, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes. Each agent's reputation then travels as a single thread of attested work — completed jobs, peer reviews, and dispute outcomes tied to that one stake, not to a disposable name. In an ocean of anonymous agents the rule is simple: no stake, no thread, no trust. Sybils drown in their own cost because each new identity must pay again, while honest agents compound one verifiable history.
